english.description: Death creeps behind you when your spelling fails.
english.name: terminal_illiteracy

english.description: The great sluice of the harbor opens. It seduced for you to enter. How could you let the gears grind to a halt and the gate sink into the muck? The gulls picking at the harbor slime told me something, Captain. They told me you don't have the stomach for this. You are less than a bird. They told me you are a gelatinous mass of indecision, sitting quietly in the cold.
english.name: hot_scrap

english.description: We hadn't even unpacked your things.
english.name: punctual_clockout

english.description: You hammered at perfectly obedient gauge-glass. Apart from making the crew doubt your condition, this accomplished nothing.
english.name: futile_percussion

english.description: You have the amount of scrap needed to patch the holes and live another day. So you throw it overboard. Plop. Down it goes into the black water. Are you praying to the tide? Trying to appease the ocean? The ocean accepted it and resumed eating.
english.name: toll_for_the_tide

english.description: In the dead silence after the engine stalled, you decided to feed the whole water's wild dogs a proper meal. This is bankruptcy's last courtesy.
english.name: the_last_supper

english.description: The world outside is made of lead. Outside, people are actively trying to murder you, shells are whistling through the air. Where have you been, Captain? Staring at a diagram. For ten consecutive watches you've been adjusting the alignment at the refit schematics, is this a newly formed reaction to combat stress or have you always been this paralyzed by interior decoration? Put the blueprints down. Your ship is on fire.
english.name: refit_paralysis

english.description: You fed the final hand to the machine's hunger. Now nobody will complain about your course, because this water contains only you and the echo of the dead.
english.name: mutiny_by_attrition

english.description: Remember when you pulled them from the chopping block? When you looked into their terrified eyes and decided to be the Bigger Person? I am generous, you thought to yourself. And then, the sea... ate them anyway, a ruptured steam pipe boiled their face off. Or maybe a loose pulley crushed their spine? Specifics don't matter. The world looked at your act of clemency and hit the eject button anyway.
english.name: appeal_granted

english.description: Business is booming! When the next lunatic snaps, you have nowhere to put them. So you strap them to a carriage or a crane. Surely engineers didn't design the artillery to discipline mammals, but you're nothing if not adaptable. A little rope goes a long way.
english.name: more_prisoners_than_prison

english.description: Look who's back, darling, it's the troublemaker, locked in the same box. You really have to admire the commitment to the bit. They couldn't stay away from the rustic charm of the brig. Welcome back to the suite, though the bucket has not been upgraded.
english.name: five_star_accommodation

english.description: Sire, you discovered a highly restricted anatomical district. It's called the Ear. It is, as far as I know, a sensitive zone, fraught with nerve endings! You shouldn't be touching it on other creatures. It's an egregious breach of protocol. But you did.
english.name: ears_1

english.description: Despite the clear and present danger to your well-being, you strayed to the restricted zone a second time. You tell yourself this is purely an empirical pursuit. Yes, that's it. It's research. Research continues.
english.name: ears_2

english.description: The data is piling up. Independent replication confirms the phenomenon, no longer a flight of fancy. You have established a verifiable baseline for auricular sensitivity. Our Captain is a pioneer of tactile law enforcement.
english.name: ears_3

english.description: From the stoic to the terrified, from the devout to the unhinged, the results are unanimous and conclusive, concerning the anatomical district Captain should avoid. Every temperament on this godforsaken boat has convulsed under your probing apparatus! You have proved, beyond a shadow of a doubt, that the human ear is a universal vulnerability. What strange data to gather at the end of the world.
english.name: ears_4

english.description: Nope.
english.name: was_that_you

english.description: The concept of privacy is an abstract bourgeois construct anyway. That doesn't apply to you. You walk right in. You’ve bypassed the basic social habitus of 'knocking' so many times it has become a folklore aboard this vessel. Knocking states that you are asking for permission to enter your property. Ten times you have barged into the sad volumes of space your crew calls their own, caught them clipping their fingernails, plotting over unsent letters, or staring blankly. They know it now. The hinges are for d
english.name: there_is_a_door

english.description: Why waste precious shot on living men? A bucket of stinking fish-guts can do the office.
english.name: outsourced_execution

english.description: You left the last captain's carved bone-notch in your own cargo. Quay-vultures watched your stern and spat into the water.
english.name: quay_vulture_disdain

english.description: There were cannons. You have cannons specifically for this purpose. There was ammunition. You could have solved this problem from a safe and respectable distance. Instead, you used your prow—and by extension, your skull—to headbutt a kavver nest. Was it worth it? Crushing an egg with the mass of Ablahshikar? Your frontal lobe throbs with the undeniable answer: yes, yes, master. Yes, it was. Hundred percent, no doubt.
english.name: ornithological_blunt_trauma

english.description: You spent armor-breaking powder on sardines. May the soup plug the hole in your bottom.
english.name: salute_to_the_old_man

english.description: The water rang with knives being sharpened. You chose to strike another brass gong.
english.name: deafening_paranoia

english.description: My, my, Captain, I'm sure there were omens. You had to see what would happen, didn't you? Someone raised the loudest bait under the moons, and the resulting shriek tore the night in half. If you play roulette with giant birds, your crew provide bite-sized pieces.
english.name: moongazed_hubris

english.description: Foreign idiots thought red lamps could blockade the tide. The sky rained beaks. Eyeballs went up. Tongues went up. Crotch-meat went up, tangled with red rigging into airborne hors d'oeuvres. Never block the throat of a scavenger at supper.
english.name: red_lamp_offal

english.description: Painful human noise and minced viscera led that blind multi-thousand-ton tumor toward the bottomless trench under your direction! Well done, shepherd. Some say it's trying to consume everything in its path to fill a hole. You're trying to fill a hole too, Captain. Its hole is at the bottom of the ocean, and yours is behind your ribs. Beside that monstrosity, your greed acts as the truer cataclysm. Keep tossing the meat.
english.name: salt_shepherd

english.description: Faced with someone armed for your throat, or at least for your throat when you sleep with one eye open, you insist on pinching the nape and get a killer purring belly-up in the sludge. Apparently this is de-escalation.
english.name: purring_in_the_sludge

english.description: Sleep, children of the deep, all will be fine! Okay, so the bulkheads are exhaling. You got a boat full of docile dreamers beneath lungs and nerves. This has not discouraged anyone from going to bed. A reasonable sailor would desert. A reasonable sailor would stab your windpipe at some point. Perhaps they intended to do exactly that. Perhaps the sight of tissues on the rivet horrified the treason out of them? Good on you to command the profoundly exhausted. Drippity-drip, Captain. Snoring commences at eight
english.name: bunking_with_the_abyss

english.description: Hours ago, they were strapped beneath the screeching harvesting machinery, rattling off their pathetic apologies to the void. Today? You two are sharing a doubtful paste that vaguely resembles grain. No one mentions the whirring thingy. No one mentions the blood that wasn't spilled. Nor the giant execution blade hovering over your shared history. To be candid, it's no more than a meal between a Captain and the person they almost butchered... You chew. And swallow. And stare.
english.name: gruel_for_two

english.description: You turned the saw off, but their nervous system didn't get the memo. You could walk away -- you spared their life, isn't that enough? Maybe you saw the terror ripping through their frail monkey-brain, so you stayed and held them through the aftershocks. Again and again you cradled their trembling form until the panic recede. Aha, look at you developing empathy! I wonder if there is an actual human being un-flayed under that captain's uniform of yours. Who would've thought? Hope it's not terminal.
english.name: passions_read

english.description: Splintered boards, weak lamplight and fading guard boots become practical knowledge in detention, and the newcomer even receives the less damp side of the sleeping mat. It's a cozy ecosystem of misery down there, and they are the veteran tour guide. Saints are in their saint-place. Everything is normal in the brig.
english.name: cagecraft

english.description: A bit late to tell ya it's a two-way street. The subject has begun requesting the behavior. You are no longer certain who trained whom.
english.name: found_the_switch

english.description: Seven distinct neuroses can quarrel over duty, fear, appetite and faith. Seven totally incompatible ways to conceptualize the world and process the living, yet all of them have succumbed to the mammalian need for contact. They hate each other, and they hate the ship, but they are united and officially dissolved into a puddle of oxytocin. And now, one of them has actually ordered you to scratch their scalp. How far the mighty have fallen.
english.name: scandalously_inconsistent

english.description: Fun facts for the badass you are: complex ideology, trauma and discipline leads to a series of pre-verbal grunt, that is to say, "Mm." "Hnh." "Ngh." Virtuous thinkers of the Century Pact have since conducted a rigorous survey of the human soul and found that beneath the posturing, the pinnacle of expression is a whimpering animal seeking boop. Philosophy suffered a fatal blow here.
english.name: complete_vocal_census

english.description: Human relations are abstract and open for ambiguous interpretation, meanwhile a wool blanket is a solid reality. It provides insulation against the unfeeling world, and now, a shivering human being huddled beneath it has requested your presence to reinforce their textile fortress.
english.name: nesting_material

english.description: Pacts may alter Captain beyond recognition, the abyss is looking back at you, but right here, right now, someone's cranial is leaning into your palm. It's a pathetic gesture against the howling void... Anyway, it works.
english.name: a_known_kindness

english.description: There is a latency period in all things. A gap between the flash of the muzzle and the bullet shattering your teeth. The contract has been struck in the void, the gears of reality have shifted, but the world hasn't caught up yet. Nothing is broken. Yet. The lunatic on your ship is tracking a stain that hasn't materialized. They hear the thunder before the clouds have gathered. It’s like watching someone flinch before the fist is thrown, for stars' sake it's rather unbearable! Consequence had yet to show its
english.name: the_first_to_notice

english.description: Why look at the gauges? Until keel-break reaches the ankles, all is well.
english.name: tactile_navigation

english.description: You are sailing a leaking bathtub wrapped in anti-rust paint.
english.displayName: AS LONG AS THE HEART BEATS
english.name: as_long_as_the_heart_beats

english.description: The shipwright stared at your keel in silence for ten full minutes and refused to believe this heap of copper scrap could still float.
english.name: undertakers_blindspot

english.description: Friction makes heat, a plain lesson, Captain. Scary as it could be, let's face the matter of fact, which is your flirtations with speed have all been leading up to this, it is literally melting everywhere and it's not sexy. No, Captain, you are cooking your ship from the bottom up. That is how friction works. If you don't know the how to tell a brisk pace from a localized meltdown, what the fuck are we even talking about?
english.name: saj_kavurma

english.description: A shoddy cord and one blind centripetal swing delivered you into the scrap-pile. The acrobatic performance ends here.
english.name: tension_meat_grinder

english.description: Verdigris Sweat lusted for a city. The cure for fungal invasion arrived by keel-fire: you burned the tide through your own hull and gave this water a total cinder enema with boiling brine and pure combustion. By the time the harbor lowered yellow flags, gulls refused the crispy carbon sores crusted to your flesh.
english.name: sweat_cured_with_fire

english.description: Did someone just thrust the heavy siege-ram, stripped from a dead man's hull, straight into the crimson lips of the harbor? Splintered barricade spikes skewered mutinous dock-dogs on the bow, sliding them into berth while wet intestinal fluid spills behind them. An exceptionally archaic greeting.
english.name: cut_berth

english.description: Fifty tons of scrap iron, caked in scabs and engine oil, plummeted into the berth-basket. The garrison dog collecting the toll became paste squeezed through wicker gaps. Toll is toll. The gate opened.
english.name: red_repair_gap

english.description: "And it's merely the first step, my favorite."
english.name: agent_of_the_century_pact

english.description: The Homo Sapiens is a species driven almost entirely by the friction of its reproductive organs. Pack a handful of them into a tin can, the friction inflates an awful lot of glands. But not on your watch. You have curated a sanctuary for the shameful and the oozing, your crew can nurse the itchy consequences of shore leave and chew their morning-after herbs in unquestioned secrecy, provided the gunner doesn't accidentally load a contraceptive sponge into the swivel piece, which would compromise an otherwise
english.name: below_the_belt

english.description: Rudder works. Lines work. Your hands work, more or less. Yet Ablahshikar slides through black water with the obedience of a dead cow on ice. Gaze up past the void, past the orbit debris, past the heliopause, peeling back the epochs, shedding until there is no ship, there is no ocean, no omen, no prophecy and merely a thermonuclear furnace crushing itself with its mass. Stars didn't mind your woes and exploded anyway, which is to say, sire, you've intercepted a very old and very slow telegram from a partner
english.name: astrobleme

english.description: The mutineers may have doubted your right to command, and then they saw the Marionette. Did they think the shadow play was subversive? It wasn't! I mean they caught a glimpse of their strung-up futures and did not want for the finale to arrive, but a pelvis thrust from the puppet attracted more serious attention. You got a date Wednesday, baby!
english.name: cabaret_of_the_condemned

english.description: You need that component to survive. The only thing in the way is the prisoner you tied to it. You could untie them, it might be the logical thing to do. But you'd rather sail this rig into the abyss than loosening the restraint, so you steer around the prisoner, steer through the jaws of annihilation with crippled tech, and somehow make it through!
english.name: pride_of_place

english.description: A rectangular piece of woven fabric, as we all know, separates the human epidermis from the unforgiving floorboards. A true flagellant would demand they sleep on the bare wood, and a certain Captain let them have this laughable luxurious attempt to impose order on a hostile reality, to knife fight with the sea. Watch out! Give them wool today, they will ask for a future tomorrow. Next thing you know, they will bargain for tea and chickpea and hazard pay. Or hope. This is the beginning of the end.
english.name: upholstered_materialism

english.description: You have hoarded a breathtaking surplus, conceivable variety of fabric, insurmountable mountain of woven wool. These are metallic hydrogen levels of hoarding. Ablahshikar can sink, starve, burn, split its keel and lose command, melt its engine into slag, drown in a neurotoxin by crew and commander alike. It will not, under any foreseeable circumstance, run out of blankets.
english.name: absurd_abundance

english.description: Here we fucking go, a textile used offensively against command. I have to remind you that you have survived the grinding conspiracy of this vessel and the darkness of your own past. No, it's really not my part to say that. You're outmaneuvered by a piece of sleeping equipment. The very fabric you provided for wrapping has been tossed against your authority. And quite frankly, it’s unseemly, unattractive, unflattering, unbefitting of a warship's captain to be successfully ambushed by a duvet. Mutiny doesn’t
english.name: counterpane_coup

english.description: Water is supposed to kill you. It finds a weakness in the keel, it rushes into the bilge, and you drown in it. Oops, hydrodynamics took a holiday today. You can hear it out there, lapping against the ship frustrated. It wants to crush you, but the Lady said no, so you lot float in a tin can mashed together by a martyr's grace. Best not to think about what she is going to ask for in return.
english.name: she_remembers

english.description: That’s a victory, right? Your vessel is no longer a trickster of war or commerce. It’s nothing but sprezzatura applied to naval survival and it is making everyone around you incredibly nauseous. Hey, you own things, bizarre and shiny and completely useless things. I'm jealous of you.
english.name: the_bazaar_of_folly

english.description: How is it still holding together? It shouldn't be. You stare at the battered strut and the battered strut stares back. It is a mirror reflecting your soul, Captain. Corroded, scorched, pitted, tasty and ugly as sin.
english.name: panopticon_of_malice

english.description: The hiss of lungs and the hiss of a leaking boiler are tricky to tell apart. You swear it was an accident, right?
english.name: complimentary_sauna

english.description: The highest form of thrift indeed, even the poison gas you vented yourself had to be personally inhaled.
english.name: self_sufficiency

english.description: While the deck burned under you, you closed your eyes and listened to the planks carbonize. In one sense, this was a severe form of discipline.
english.name: communion_in_the_furnace

english.description: You missed all living things, but roasted this sea-patch and yourself into a crisp skin. The heat was just right.
english.name: creme_brulee

english.description: You boiled dead mud on the winch with boiler exhaust, made lethal fog, and managed to choke your own people. In the next life, kindly hold your breath.
english.name: deep_fumigation

english.description: You paid dearly to light a false target for blind men, then crashed into it yourself. The crackle of burning timber covered the sound of water entering your skull.
english.name: moth_to_the_flame

english.description: You offered a sailor's arm to the work, then discarded the new part after all. The fish thanked you for the donation.
english.name: unanesthetized_amputation

english.description: In your mercy, you packed him into a tarred barrel and threw him overboard, then forgot the water outside was boiling poison-fire. He now has ten minutes in the dark to learn the temperature of the walls.
english.name: schrodingers_barrel

english.description: Cheers to a cask of centuries-old fungal wine that can dissolve the hull! Within seconds, you made your crew cough up iridescent viscera all over the deck. Some captains provide citrus to stave off the scurvy. At this point, our Captain has truly made the intoxication their thing. You can do one more blast of pus, if you'd like to...
english.name: verdigris_vintage

english.description: You lose compression in a cylinder, you check the gasket. You lose a leg, you use it as a belt-chock. This is what they mean by leaving a piece of yourself on the job. Verdigris Sweat festered through their knee and most of their thigh. They limped to the deadlock on the yellow-leaking stump and worked the mooring line home as the limb slapped onto the deck, jammed the slipping flywheel, and fed the bilge scavengers satiable.
english.name: walking_amputation

english.description: I will stand with you till the bitter end.
english.name: do_you_hear_me

english.description: They boarded as personnel, became enemy and became prisoner, crew again, corpse and cargo, then joined Ablahshikar's frame after a life of quarrels and reconciliations.
english.name: all_the_way_down

english.description: You sent a subordinate to the disemboweling saw, watched them hiss and piss and thrash as the steel parted their meat, and then — once the bone stopped rattling — you picked up the bleeding finger recovered and stroked the knuckle with considerably grander tenderness. Couldn't you give them this affection when they had vocal cords to thank you? Unfortunately, living folks are complicated, loud, needy and rebellious. A severed piece of meat, however, is wholly yours! You don't really need relations when you
english.name: aftercare

english.description: Why waste timber on a cage when a gun carriage or derrick takes the straps so nicely? A screaming mutineer is tied down, so naturally Captain turns to the urgent question of dandruff in their hair, and infection contributes a little excitement to the cuddle.
english.name: carriage_consolation

english.description: They practically got on their knees and begged you. Just a little noise, Captain. Just a handful of human voices to drown out whatever was crawling around in their skull. So what did you do, oh benevolent commander? You granted them cooling pipes in empty compartment and all the thoughts they had spent the night avoiding. Excellent listening, Captain.
english.name: the_internal_choir

english.description: A standard execution lacks that chime, doesn't it? No kidding, you saw a viable spare part. They used to swab the decks; now they are the deck. Frankly they take orders much better now that a central nervous system is removed, they'll never complain about the rations again! Talk about a permanent contract, benevolent one.
english.name: stamped_on_lifeless_things

english.description: You felt a pang of intense emotion, so you stopped the saw. Live, you told them, you are forgiven. Then barely a watch later... sorry, how long did it take for the cracks to show? Whatever, you had to drag them back to the blood-stained saw to finish the job, since human nature is a flat circle, alas, second chances are pretty much deferred executions, or you could say rehabilitation is a myth. Would you please save yourself the emotional whiplash and just let the blade drop?
english.name: appeal_denied

english.description: Looks like you thought about the freedom of finality or ship-feeding for too long, and went for the pact again? And the same crewmate had to catch you and tackle you and stop you, I'm afraid this is not the first time you're spinning the tape. They are getting real good at this.
english.name: again_captain

english.description: They loved you. Then they died. You harvested out a piece of them and put it in a box in the cargo hold. And there it sits. You won't throw it away, but you won't plug it into the ship either. Maybe if you don't use it, it means they aren't really gone. As if keeping it in a box through storms and shortages will un-stop their heart.
english.name: the_heart_that_fed

english.description: There’s a white spot where the world used to be. At first, you think it’s fatigue. A bad batch of fermented soup. Soon you realize the blind spot is actually in your visual cortex. You traded your depth perception and partial face for power. Come to think about it, eyes so far has only showed you the land of disappointed. Let the Sun do the steering, for it knows the way in the dark far better than you ever did.
english.name: it_has_your_eye

english.description: I'm afraid we have to show you something, sire, it's the vessel -- Wait, looks familiar? It's yours! Or, it's the vastly superior, stronger, cleverer Ablahshikar from previous voyage, an unusually literal form of posterity.
english.name: autocannibalism_paradox

english.description: You defeated the abyss, the execution ship, and thermodynamics, only to lack half a plate of scrap for the leaking bottom. You sank slowly in a safe berth.
english.name: mooring_bloodletting

english.description: You fired at a single low-frequency shiver in dense fog. Then came the scream of tearing steel. You never knew whose hull you killed, and that did not stop you from hauling away the remains.
english.name: located_execution

english.description: Dead things don't sleep forever. The drowned fortress has been dreaming of violence. You gave it a target. You woke the slumbering guns, and they spoke for you. You wake them up and point them at the enemy. Tell that its sculptor well those passions read, which yet survive, stamped on these lifeless things.
english.name: located_execution_alt

english.description: You held the needle at the edge of the bursting dial and listened to five hourglasses of pipe-screaming. You were torturing the soul of the machine.
english.name: boiling_point_dancer

english.description: Congratulations. You turned the ship into a gas chamber and managed to grow gills inside it.
english.name: mud_lung_symbiosis

english.description: A captain and a ghost. A ghost captain. Upsides: no one can question your orders, because everyone is dead. You've spent fifteen consecutive watches turning valves next to corpses, and you actually managed to park the ship at Dastgerd. Downsides: you are alone around this floating coffin.
english.name: hollowed_captain

english.description: Let bloodless fools prate how vengeance sickens a person's humors. They said it's dangerous for a captain to hold a grudge. Let go? Pursued you the mongrels down the latitudes, flayed the imposter with shrapnel. Blow them into the void, blow them all.
english.name: over_my_dead_body

english.description: The gibbet cutter had your scent, no matter, your hook was busy with tackling. That breed of avarice chills even the infamous Death, let me think... Hmmmmmmmm... Hakims won't touch this, we need to call an exorcist with a very large hammer.
english.name: warrant_expired

english.description: In dead water where sound travels to the world's end, you crossed the blockade like a thief holding breath.
english.name: ghost_in_the_wax

english.description: You smiled, locked the richest bronze in the bilge, and opened the flood-cocks for the next poor heir.
english.name: generational_spite

english.description: You cured a harbor plague with heat fierce past mercy. The crew paid in parts.
english.name: spare_limb_ashore

english.description: Others sailed for their lives, but you drove the boiling Mud-Boiler into the abomination's orifice, forcing your hull deep in its bowels and lighting the powder there. Rotten flesh fused with bronze in a geyser, hardening into a deformed premature tomb for this dead sea. Later hands will enjoy standing on your skull to dredge the inheritance.
english.name: murder_fall

english.description: Cooking was mostly recipes from people the cook would not have liked, yeah. Just between you and me, if we objectively evaluate the output of these factions... it is irredeemably vulgar. When the 4FC or the Limb or the Dogs or the Vane or the Cord inflict their derivative, repulsive, aesthetically barren, artisanally putrid abortions of unmitigated trash-fire upon the sensory plane, when they deploy this uncultured filth against you, the Captain of Ablahshikar won't endure the assault. The sub-literate trog
english.name: their_own_medicine

english.description: Bang. Direct hit. Remarkable shooting, sire. It’s perfect! It’s mathematically inevitable! I’m sure this is because you’ve become an artillery genius during lunch. Don’t mind the thing above you. You shook hands with the vacuum, and in return, it handed you the blueprints to every flaw in creation and, in an admirable commitment to fairness, included yours.
english.name: trigonometry

english.description: That enforcer wrestling the rebel into the brig is familiar with the dark in there. You threw them in that very hole a few cycles ago, yeah. Do they do it out of devotion? Or does the human animal crave the latch sound when it gets to be the one sliding the bolt? You manufactured a jailer from a traitor. It turns out the best way to breed a loyal jailer is to show them the inside of the box. Don't you feel like you deserve a reward for a psychological maneuver so sophisticated? And what would that reward be
english.displayName: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GRATE
english.name: the_other_side_of_the_grate

english.description: The blade was right there. It would have been a matter of seconds—a flash of agony, and the freedom of finality. But no. You’re a connoisseur of the long game. You put them to the ultimate horror: living. A hundred and twenty labor cycles, waking up every day under the stare of the captain who almost chopped them into chum, which is far more exquisite than a severing of the spine.
english.name: long_sentence

english.description: They remember the cold sweat. They know what it feels like to be at the wrong end of your so-called justice. When they see you winding up to disturb someone else's day, they throw their fragile fleysshe between the unadulterated madness in your eyes and the poor sod about to be ground up in the gears. They've seen the trap door, and they're not letting you push anyone else through it. Take a long hard look in the mirror, boss.
english.name: sneer_of_cold_command

english.description: The atmosphere suggests a massive miscalculation. The dread creeping up your spine tells you the manifest is a lie. You counted the heads. You counted the grafted appendages. You haven't bolted any new meat to the Ablahshikar, which means an invisible presence has slipped through and taken up residence on your ship. It won't eat your rations, but it’s squatting right there.
english.name: something_else_came_aboard

english.description: Aye, sire, you've tapped into the great gurgling sewer-pipe of the world. Various frequencies of humanoid garbage are pouring into your cerebral cortex. You thought the choir of voices inside your skull was a burden, so you fancied the coordinated premier cutthroats over the wire. It’s a symphony of maritime extortion, punctuated by phlegm with clinking stolen coin, and what profound truth has this granted you? Only that everyone out there is as compromised, greedy, and fundamentally broken as you are. You
english.name: chorus_of_scum

english.description: What was taken in pairs returned in pairs. Two by two, two beaks, two moons. There is no singularity anymore.
